clue.text: Do wrong and that's how you have to walk the plank

definitions.meaning: to commit a crime or sin, as an offender does

definitions.text: that's how you have to walk the plank
definitions.meaning: a pirate's victim walks along the board and drops off its far tip, read as two words

explanation.surface: A pirate tells a captive that misbehaving earns a stroll along the plank.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into OFF END: the plank is walked until you step off its end.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress or break a law is the verb sense, synonymous with doing wrong.

clue.text: Unit of work on short time?

definitions.text: Unit of work on short time?

parts.note: the foot-pound is an imperial measure of energy expended in lifting
a second is a brief moment

explanation.surface: Sounds like a worker put on reduced hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot-pound-second is the old British system of units built on the foot, the pound and the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the imperial measuring system, combining a work measure with a time measure.

clue.text: Record of inflammation it is not

indicators.note: says the words it is are to be absent from the inflammation's name

parts.note: enteritis is swelling of the intestine
taken as written, the letters to be dropped

explanation.surface: A medical note insisting a condition is not inflammation.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something in a ledger or log is to put it down in writing, a synonym.

clue.text: 13 with ice?

parts.note: 13 across means fitted; ice is slang for diamonds, so fitted with diamonds, or in card terms holding that suit

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that reads like a drink order on the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Set with gems, jewellery is diamond-studded; ice is underworld slang for those stones.

clue.text: Personal airline?

parts.note: an airline is read not as a carrier but as a line, or tube, carrying air inside one's own body

explanation.surface: A private jet company for one person.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the tube conducting breath to the lungs, a private conduit for air.

clue.text: What may be given to those departed from the wars?

definitions.text: What may be given to those departed

indicators.note: says the letters of the following words are made out of, reshaped from, them

explanation.surface: A remembrance of soldiers who died in conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is the weak anagram signal: the letters of THE WARS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral rings are laid at funerals and memorials as tributes to the dead.

clue.text: Restraint for animal, or ring in its place for a bull

indicators.note: puts the ring letter inside the bull's snout word

parts.note: a bull's ring goes through its snout
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Choices for controlling livestock: a halter, or a ring through a bull's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope tightening when pulled can tether or catch a beast, as a lasso does.

clue.text: Average goddess curtailed by new arrival

parts.note: par is the norm or standard level

indicators.note: a tail cut off means the goddess loses her final letter

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love

explanation.surface: An ordinary goddess pushed aside by a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart, someone newly risen in society, is the French-derived term for a recent social arrival.

clue.text: Never-ending Synod agenda item on women bishops?

definitions.text: Never-ending Synod agenda item on women bishops?

parts.words: Never-ending Synod agenda item on women bishops?
parts.note: the Church of England's General Synod debated women bishops for years; a proposal put to a meeting is a motion, and this one seemed endless

explanation.surface: A jibe at the Church of England's long-running debate over ordaining women as bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine running forever without energy input is the physicist's impossible dream; here it is an endless proposal.

clue.text: Snake path that winds on the river

parts.note: a boa is a constricting serpent
a trace is a track or trail

explanation.surface: A serpent's trail meandering along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on a winding stretch of the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous university rowing event follows a curving course along the Thames, so it winds on that river.

clue.text: Model of spheres, or about railway termini

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the end stations of a line are its outer points, so the railway word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: A model of globes, or something to do with station ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A clockwork device showing planets circling the sun is a working model of the heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Box returning sharp blows

indicators.note: has the word for sharp knocks come back the other way

parts.note: raps are quick knocks

explanation.surface: A boxer hitting back with quick punches.
explanation.definitionFit: To box lightly in practice, exchanging punches with a partner, is a synonym.

clue.text: Not sliding downwards, unlikely even to hell

indicators.note: an improbable arrangement means the letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A sinner hoping not to slip downhill to perdition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and horizontal, nothing slopes so nothing slides; the idiom also means honest.

clue.text: Fitted to abandon duties

indicators.note: read as wild abandon, it means the letters are thrown loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fit for the job walks away from responsibilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropriate or well matched, as clothing tailored to someone; a synonym.

clue.text: Nudge — it's about a Greek letter — first letter to the Guardian

indicators.note: turns the letters of it's round

parts.note: taken as its letters
mu is the twelfth character of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word letter

parts.note: the setter writes in the Guardian, so the paper is us

explanation.surface: A prompt to the newspaper concerning Greek, sent as a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IT'S to STI; the Guardian is the paper speaking, so 'the Guardian' gives US.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur or prompt to act is a synonym for a gentle push.

clue.text: Fashion in setter's slum shows lack of delicacy

indicators.note: places the fashion word inside the run made from setter's and slum

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I'M, I am
a sty is a filthy dwelling
a mode is a style or vogue

explanation.surface: A setter's untidy home dressed up fashionably looks indelicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamelessness or want of modesty is a coarseness, the opposite of delicacy.

clue.text: Extra turmoil of Dum and Dee — the latter curtailed

indicators.note: an upheaval throws the letters into a new order
the latter is Dee, the second of the pair named; curtailed cuts off its tail letter

explanation.surface: A spot of trouble between Tweedledum and Tweedledee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the latter curtailed' trims DEE to DE, and 'turmoil' rearranges DUM, AND and DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added at the end of a book or document is a supplement or extra part.

clue.text: Offensive term has to stop before one address to dignitary

indicators.note: puts the first pieces ahead of the one

parts.note: eff is the euphemism for a swear word
end means halt
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Instructions for swearing to cease before speaking to someone important.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turkish title of respect, used for a man of standing, is a form of address to an official.

clue.text: Appease a girl, if she'll come round

indicators.note: the girl wraps herself round the word if

parts.note: Molly is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Pacifying a girl in the hope she will relent.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or pacify anger is to placate, a synonym.

clue.text: Just depend on Gordius!

indicators.note: in an across answer the depending word sits after the setter

parts.note: Gordius is the setter, who refers to himself as me
rely means depend

explanation.surface: A setter's cheeky boast: you can always count on me.
explanation.definitionFit: Only or simply, as in no more than; a synonym for the adverb.

clue.text: Three-quarters canine drew to latest fashion

parts.note: three of the four compass quarters: north, east and west
a canine is a pointed tooth, a fang
led, as in drew a crowd

explanation.surface: A dog breed bred for the newest trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel and modish, often disparagingly; the adjective describes something in the newest style.

clue.text: Lifting a great weight is false

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting lets the letters read upwards

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a ton is a heavy measure

explanation.surface: A weightlifter claiming a heavy load that is not genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a retort meaning untrue, contradicting a claim.

clue.text: There's no winter without including some precipitation

indicators.note: the outer words contain, or include, the precipitation

explanation.surface: A complaint that a winter without snowfall is no winter at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen flakes falling from clouds are one form of moisture from the sky.

clue.text: What it all adds up to in Greek?

definitions.text: What it all adds up to in Greek?

parts.words: What it all adds up to in Greek?
parts.note: the mathematician's sign for a total is a Greek capital letter

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about the meaning of everything, asked in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter S, as a capital, is the summation symbol in mathematics.

clue.text: Lines for a boy about 10?

parts.note: a son is a boy child

indicators.note: about in the sense of turned about, so the number word is read from its end backwards

parts.note: ten in words

explanation.surface: Writing lines as punishment for a boy of about ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourteen-line poem is a set of verse lines, so lines can define it.

clue.text: One gains in collecting badges of office

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: gathering up the letters and putting them together anew signals rearrangement

explanation.surface: An official accumulating emblems of rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia or emblems denoting rank or authority, as worn by officials.

clue.text: In the position of a back-seat driver?

definitions.text: In the position of a back-seat driver?

parts.words: In the position of a back-seat driver?
parts.note: a back-seat driver gives unwanted counsel, so is placed in a counselling role

explanation.surface: Describes the seating of a nagging passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: Offering counsel without authority to act is consultative, like an interfering passenger.

clue.text: Hankers after a name in time

indicators.note: puts the name letter inside the time word

parts.note: years means a span of time

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a name that will last through time.
explanation.definitionFit: To long or pine for something is to crave it, a synonym.
